- **Assumption:** $500/$1,500/$5,000 are **upfront hardware budgets**, USD, excluding colocation. These are planning estimates, **not verified 2026 quotes**. Hardware alone cannot guarantee 1,000 concurrent players.

- **$500:** used Ryzen **5 5600/5600X**, **32GB DDR4**, **1TB NVMe**, consumer motherboard/case/PSU. Plausible budget build; least headroom for crowded hubs, scripts, and database activity.

- **$1,500:** Ryzen **7 9700X**, **64GB DDR5**, **2TB TLC NVMe**, good cooling. Best-balanced tier; prioritize sustained single-thread performance over additional cores.

- **$5,000:** Ryzen **9 9950X**, **128GB DDR5**, **2×2TB NVMe mirrored**, UPS, plus backup/spare hardware. Extra cores help auxiliary workloads—not proportional realm capacity. Mirroring isn’t backup.

- **Bandwidth:** provision **1Gbps**, DDoS protection, and substantial transfer allowance. Assuming—not measuring—**5–20KB/s outbound/player**, 1,000 continuously connected players produce **40–160Mbps**, approximately **13–52TB/month**. Measure your actual workload.

- **Cloud comparison:** historical AWS **us-east-1 Linux m7i.2xlarge**, **8 vCPU/32GiB**, **$0.4032/hour ≈ $294/month**; **1TiB gp3 ≈ $82/month**. Internet egress at **$0.09/GB** implies roughly **$1,170–$4,680/month before tiers/free allowances**. Shared vCPUs aren’t equivalent to dedicated physical cores.

- **Factorio:** deterministic lockstep; clients execute the simulation from synchronized player actions. Replay requires matching game/mod versions and initial state. [Documentation](https://wiki.factorio.com/Replay_system).
- **Supreme Commander: Forged Alliance / FAF:** shipped RTS with deterministic simulation and command-stream replays; desynchronization and version compatibility remain practical constraints. [FAF game code](https://github.com/FAForever/fa).
- **OpenRA:** released open-source RTS engine; synchronized orders, deterministic simulation, replay recording, synchronization checks. [Source](https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA).
- **Spring / Beyond All Reason:** synchronized simulation, recorded demos, desync diagnostics; separates synchronized gameplay from unsynchronized UI/rendering. [BAR engine](https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/spring).
- **Age of Empires II / Warcraft III:** shipped lockstep RTS implementations with action-based recorded games/replays; not portable recordings across arbitrary engine patches.
- **Techniques:** record initial snapshot, tick-indexed inputs, external events, exact executable/content versions, and RNG seeds/state. Periodically hash canonical simulation state **including RNG state**; RNG-only hashes miss other divergence. Stable entity iteration, deterministic job ordering, and controlled script execution matter.
- **Float traps:** x87 versus SSE precision, FMA contraction, compiler reassociation, platform math libraries, unordered reductions. [Concrete analysis](https://gafferongames.com/post/floating_point_determinism/).
- **MMO scale:** no verified public full-world tick-replay implementation to name confidently. **EVE Online** and **Hadean/CCP Aether Wars** demonstrate large authoritative simulations—not evidence of deterministic input-only replay.

  - `Warden.NumMemChecks`, `Warden.NumOtherChecks`
  - `Warden.ClientResponseDelay`, `Warden.ClientCheckHoldOff`
  - `Warden.ClientCheckFailAction`, `Warden.BanDuration`

- **Important distinction:** Warden performs client-integrity checks; it is **not** server-authoritative movement validation. Effective coverage depends on configured checks, client/platform support and enforcement settings. Movement handling also must accommodate legitimate teleports, transports, knockbacks and latency.

- **Opposing tools:** **WoWEmuHacker**, **Cheat Engine** and **WPE Pro** are historical names associated with private-server cheating or manipulation. - **Exposed surface:** [Eluna API reference](https://elunaluaengine.github.io/): `RegisterPlayerEvent`, `RegisterCreatureEvent`, `RegisterCreatureGossipEvent`, `RegisterServerEvent`; `Player:AddItem`, `Player:Teleport`, `Unit:CastSpell`, `WorldObject:SpawnCreature`; `WorldDBQuery`/`WorldDBExecute`. Availability depends on compiled bindings—not every C++ method is exposed.

- **Pure-Lua example:** `lua_scripts/broodlord.lua` adds periodic Frostbolts to existing creature template **12017**, Broodlord Lashlayer:
  ```lua
  local function bolt(_, _, _, c)
      local victim = c:GetVictim()
      if victim then c:CastSpell(victim, 116, true) end
  end
  RegisterCreatureEvent(12017, 1, function(_, c)
      c:RegisterEvent(bolt, 8000, 0)
  end)
  local function stop(_, c) c:RemoveEvents() end
  RegisterCreatureEvent(12017, 2, stop)
  RegisterCreatureEvent(12017, 4, stop)
  ```
  Existing template/spell required; no C++ or database changes. This augments—not replaces—existing AI.

- **Performance ceiling:** No defensible universal NPC count. Profile your build. Blocking queries and high-frequency callbacks consume server-update time; Lua is not an asynchronous job system.

- **Still C++:** Unexposed hooks/methods, packet handling changes, pathfinding internals, combat-formula changes: implement C++ modules/core patches or extend bindings. New static templates generally require SQL; new client-visible assets require client changes, not merely C++.

- **Yuzu forks — May 2024:** Nintendo’s GitHub takedown reached **8,535 repositories**, including forks. Notices: [github/dmca](https://github.com/github/dmca). Repository removal is not a judicial finding against each implementation.

- **Suyu — March 21, 2024:** GitLab removed its repository following a DMCA notice. Nintendo’s authorship of that particular notice was not publicly established; distinguish reported removal from confirmed Nintendo litigation.

- **Ryujinx — October 1, 2024:** Development/downloads stopped after Nintendo contacted developer **gdkchan**, according to the team. No publicly disclosed complaint or judgment accompanied that announcement. Ryujinx was independent, not Yuzu-derived.

- **Server reimplementations:** No new 2024–2026 server-specific action I can reliably identify. Relevant precedents remain *Davidson v. Jung*, **422 F.3d 630 (8th Cir. 2005)**—**bnetd**—and *MDY v. Blizzard*, **629 F.3d 928 (9th Cir. 2010)**.

- **Practical §1201 posture:** Clean-room development helps copyright defenses, not automatic circumvention immunity. **§1201(f)** provides conditional interoperability protection; bypassing authentication/access controls or distributing circumvention tools remains separately risky. Preservation exemptions are narrow, not general public-server authorization.

No listed artifact type makes backflow mandatory. **Being generated does not confer authority.** A computed value can become canonical through an authorized state transition; that is not permission to synchronize build output over its inputs.

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Checked-in generated code must overwrite its source inputs | Disputed |
| A lockfile may canonically record an authorized dependency resolution | Supported |
| Checksums may canonically attest an accepted release | Supported |
| Generated docs must overwrite their authoring sources | Disputed |
| Hash-chain integrity proves a content update was authorized or current | Disputed |
| This fleet requires any particular generated artifact to become canonical | Unproven |

### Decision rule

Backflow is **required only when the governing schema or workflow requires recording a computed result as authoritative**, and delegates that transition to a specified writer. Otherwise it is merely permitted—or forbidden—not mandatory.

Allow that transition only when all these conditions hold:

1. **Declared authority:** The destination, fields, writer, and triggering event are explicitly authorized. “The build produced it” is insufficient.
2. **Bound provenance:** The candidate identifies its canonical input revision, relevant external inputs, and generating procedure.
3. **Freshness:** Acceptance checks that the relevant canonical inputs still match that revision. Stale candidates are rejected or recomputed—not silently copied.
4. **Bounded mutation:** Only delegated fields or artifacts change. Generated docs cannot incidentally replace hand-authored sources.
5. **Auditable acceptance:** The accepted change and its provenance are recorded through the ledger’s canonical commit protocol; existing ledger entries remain untouched.

**Falsifier for this rule:** A stale candidate, unauthorized writer, or out-of-scope mutation passes these gates and becomes canonical. Test all three, including a concurrent canonical edit between generation and acceptance.

The rollback case fails because output freshness or write authority was substituted for canonical authority. A drift guard alone does not establish the missing authorization.

### Amended FX5

> Canonical state governs derivation. Derived artifacts MUST NOT overwrite canonical state through ordinary synchronization. Computed results MAY enter canonical state only through an explicitly delegated, provenance-bound, freshness-checked, scope-limited, ledger-recorded acceptance transition. They MUST do so only where the governing workflow requires that record. Such acceptance grants authority to the recorded result, not to its build directory or to reverse synchronization generally.

**Falsifier for the amendment:** A compliant execution can silently replace newer canonical content with older derived content.

No task-size break-even is established. Minutes, calls, and lanes are proxies; audit value also depends on consequence and reconstructability.

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Receipt overhead exceeds audit value below a known task size | Unproven |
| A five-minute cutoff is an economically optimal threshold | Unproven |
| The following threshold is suitable as a falsifiable trial rule | Unproven |

**Concrete trial threshold:** lightweight receipts suffice only when **all** conditions hold:

- Planned execution time **≤5 minutes**.
- **Zero external calls**, excluding required ledger operations.
- **One lane** touched.
- No deletion, permission change, secret access, spending, publication, or irreversible action.
- Task is independently reversible; splitting a larger operation into smaller tasks does not establish eligibility.

This deliberately makes consequence a gate, not something averaged away by short duration.

**Amendment wording**

> Before execution, append a hash-chained receipt identifying the actor, task, parent operation, lane, authorized scope, execution cap, expected effects, and applicable falsifier version.
>
> A lightweight receipt is permitted only under the trial eligibility conditions above. All other tasks require the full receipt.
>
> Before exceeding any declared boundary, pause and append a full receipt authorizing the expanded scope. Expiration of the five-minute execution cap requires the same transition.
>
> On completion or abandonment, append an outcome record identifying resulting artifacts, reversals, and deviations. Never overwrite prior records.
>
> Commit evaluation criteria before collecting trial data. Lightweight status waives supplementary documentation, not preauthorization, chain integrity, or outcome recording.

**Committed falsifiers**

| Proposed rule | Failure that falsifies it |
|---|---|
| Lightweight records preserve sufficient auditability | One eligible task leaves actor, authorization, affected artifacts, or event order materially ambiguous where the prescribed full receipt would have resolved it. |
| Eligibility gates contain risk | One compliant eligible task causes an irreversible or cross-lane effect despite satisfying the gates. |
| Five minutes is a useful operational cutoff | In a precommitted trial of 200 eligible tasks, measured documentation-time savings are no greater than additional audit and recovery time attributable to lightweight records. |

Passing those tests would support continued use—not establish an economic optimum. Price audit losses explicitly before claiming a cost-benefit break-even.

The context cannot establish that any rule was **never** amended, or what the fleet **did not send**. Answering either as fact would invent evidence.

### 1. What is it believing that it has not tested?

These are untested in the supplied record—not necessarily untested by the fleet.

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Five green harnesses establish reliability beyond those harnesses. | **Unproven** |
| A hash-chained ledger establishes truth, not merely consistency with a retained chain head. | **Disputed** |
| A hash-committed key establishes an independent, uncontaminated, representative blind challenge. | **Unproven** |
| The tested referee chain will deliver correct operational judgments through the two-click gate. | **Unproven** |
| Crossing its kill line conditionally refutes the favorite theory under its chosen test. | **Supported**, as reported |
| That refutation establishes a general capacity to abandon favored beliefs. | **Unproven** |

The largest gap: **internal discipline is being offered without evidence of external validity.** Green tests, commitments, and self-refutation can all coexist with a badly chosen measurement system.

Proposed test: an independently administered, previously inaccessible challenge with frozen scoring and predefined failure thresholds. **Falsifier of claimed generalization:** performance below those thresholds.

### 2. Which rule has never once been amended?

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Append-only operation is a stated current rule. | **Supported** |
| Append-only operation—or any other rule—has never been amended. | **Unproven** |
| An immutable record implies immutable governance. | **Disputed** |

You need the founding rules and complete amendment history. Append-only records can record rule changes perfectly well.

Proposed audit: trace every current rule through versioned governance records. **Falsifier of “never amended”:** one authenticated prior version with substantively different requirements. Missing history leaves the claim unproven.

### 3. What would a stranger adopt first—and what was missing?

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| A stranger’s actual first choice is knowable here. | **Unproven** |
| A particular artifact was omitted from an unseen shipment. | **Unproven** |

**Candidate first adoption:** a standalone ledger verifier with valid and deliberately corrupted fixtures—not the fleet’s theory or Discord ceremony.

**What this account lacks:** the executable evidence package: verifier, schemas, fixtures, frozen scoring rules, and independently retained chain-head commitments.

**Adoption test:** give that package to a stranger without operator assistance. **Falsifier of portability:** they cannot reproduce verdicts or detect the planted corruptions.

The binomial law requires future targets to be **independent fair bits conditional on the entire committed record**. “Generated later” alone does not establish that.

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Arbitrary fixed past bits give \(K\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(1024,1/2)\) under that conditional-randomness assumption | Supported |
| \(K\ge563\) has one-sided null probability below 0.001 | Supported |
| A public hash alone proves commitment preceded target generation | Disputed |
| This particular box satisfies the randomness and chronology assumptions | Unproven |

Costs below are incremental cash, excluding labor. Each hardening includes a rejection condition—its operational falsifier—not proof that undetected cheating is impossible.

| Failure | How it fakes a pass | Cheapest hardening / rejection condition | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Custodian collusion | Custodian permits substitution or falsely attests chronology. Collusion alone cannot defeat an independently anchored, binding hash. | Give identical records to two independent recipients; publicly anchor the digest before targets. Reject inconsistent copies or missing pre-target receipts. | $0; coordination |
| Hash does not prove timing | Digest is published after targets, backdated, or selected from many candidate commitments. | Register one eligible digest, session ID, length and encoding in an independently timestamped append-only record before target release. Reject late or multiple eligible commitments. | $0–few dollars |
| Coin bias | If past bits favor the coin’s favored outcome, expected matches exceed 512. | Use a preregistered independent target source with an explicit fairness assumption; audit outcome frequencies separately. Reject protocol deviations; detected bias falsifies fairness, but passing a bias test does not establish it. | $0; recording time |

### First principles

For an immutable cohort of \(N\) seeded tasks, let \(D_N(t)\) count genuinely completed tasks:

\[
F_N(t)=D_N(t)/N,\qquad
t_{1/2}=\inf\{t:F_N(t)\ge 1/2\}.
\]

Neither quantity follows without service times, dependencies, operator availability, and a completion-validation rule.

Two incompatible laws fit the **additional assumption** that exactly 40 of the original 50 tasks genuinely finish by day 2:

| Conditional law | Fraction completed | 50-task half-life |
|---|---|---|
| Constant per-task hazard | \(F_N(t)=1-e^{-\lambda t}\), \(\lambda=\ln(5)/2\) | \(2\ln2/\ln5=0.861\) days |
| Constant crew throughput | \(F_N(t)=\min(20t/N,1)\) | \(1.25\) days |

The exponential law describes an expected fraction under a stochastic hazard model—not a guarantee. Its falsifier is a statistically incompatible completion-time distribution. The throughput law’s falsifier is sustained, measured throughput incompatible with 20 genuine completions/day while work remains available. Matching one checkpoint validates neither.

| 20 | 80% expected; 0.861 days | 100%; 0.5 days |
| 100 | 80% expected; 0.861 days | 40%; 2.5 days |

Constant hazard assumes aggregate throughput scales with board size. Constant throughput assumes crew capacity does not. Your crew description establishes neither.

The false premise is that some artifact class inherently **must** flow backward. None does. Generation confers no authority. The legitimate exception is **explicit promotion of a derived candidate into authoritative state**, not reverse synchronization.

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Generated code or docs must overwrite their canonical inputs | Disputed |
| Checked-in generated code/docs may be required repository artifacts without becoming canonical inputs | Supported |
| A generated lockfile may become authoritative for subsequent dependency resolution after acceptance | Supported |
| A checksum manifest may become an authoritative release record after acceptance; checksums alone establish neither correctness nor approval | Supported |
| The direction inversion and drift guard prevent further rollbacks in this fleet | Unproven |
| An append-only hash chain proves that recorded content was correct or authorized | Disputed |

### Decision rule

Backflow is required **only when an explicit authority policy requires accepting computed results as a new canonical decision or record**. Otherwise, derivation remains one-way.

Permit that promotion only if:

1. **Authority is scoped:** policy identifies the fields/artifacts eligible for promotion and the authorized approver or automated acceptance rule.
2. **Provenance is bound:** the candidate identifies its canonical input revisions and generation context.
3. **Freshness is checked atomically:** acceptance verifies the relevant inputs and destination still match the candidate’s declared baseline; changed state requires regeneration or explicit reconciliation.
4. **The change is intentional:** the accepted diff is recorded as a canonical transition, including any deliberately authorized rollback—not disguised as “sync.”
5. **History survives:** the ledger appends the transition, its authorization, and its predecessor; it does not rewrite earlier entries.

**Falsifier for this rule:** a stale or unauthorized candidate can overwrite current canonical content while satisfying all five conditions. That would show the conditions or their authority scope are insufficient.

The reported rollback case was an artifact’s existence being treated as overwrite authority. A drift guard helps, but does not itself establish authorization.

### Amended FX5

> Canonical authority flows to derived artifacts. Derived artifacts shall not overwrite canonical state merely because they were generated, checked in, or found different. A derived candidate may become canonical only through an explicitly authorized, provenance-bound, atomic promotion against a verified baseline, recorded as a new ledger transition. Where canonical acceptance policy requires that promotion, it must occur through that path—not reverse synchronization.

**Falsifier for the amendment’s enforcement:** a build or sync operation changes canonical state without the required promotion record, or accepts a candidate against a mismatched baseline.

### First principles

For the original seeded cohort of \(N\) tasks, define
\[
F_N(t)=\frac{\text{tasks completed by }t}{N}.
\]
The completion half-life is the time when \(F_N(t)=1/2\). Tombstoning is **not** completion; re-seeding must not erase the original denominator.

Determining \(F_N\) requires service times, operator attention, dependencies, and concurrency effectiveness—not merely lane counts.

### Conditional exponential law

**Assume** receipts certify completion and every unfinished task has constant completion hazard \(\lambda\):
\[
F_N(t)=1-e^{-\lambda t},\qquad h=\frac{\ln2}{\lambda}.
\]

Calibrating to the gate’s **boundary**, not an observed outcome:
\[
F_{50}(2)=0.8
\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{\ln5}{2},
\qquad h=\frac{2\ln2}{\ln5}\approx0.861\text{ days}.
\]

Under this model, passing the gate requires \(h\le0.861\) days. **Falsifier:** repeated cohort measurements showing nonconstant log-unfinished slopes, beyond sampling variation.

### Why board-size predictions remain conditional

An equally boundary-compatible, fixed-throughput model is
\[
F_N(t)=\min(20t/N,1),\qquad h_N=N/40.
\]
**Falsifier:** measured completion increments systematically incompatible with 20 tasks/day while work remains available.
